# rxet: Native R Bindings to Hugging Face Xet Storage

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

rxet reads files from [Hugging Face Hub](https://huggingface.co/) through Xet, the Hub's content-addressed storage engine. A single blocking Rust client, bound to R with extendr, fetches the bytes and returns them to R. Downloads to disk land in a temporary file beside `dest_path` and are renamed into place only on success, so a failed download leaves an existing file untouched.

Every call blocks the calling R thread. There is no async API.

## Installation

Needs R >= 4.3 and Rust >= 1.85 (from [rustup.rs](https://rustup.rs/)). The first build downloads and compiles the `hf-xet` crate, which takes several minutes.

```sh
R CMD INSTALL .
```

## Authentication

The CAS server rejects a raw Hub token. Call the Hub's `xet-read-token` endpoint with your Hub token and pass the `accessToken` it returns, along with its `casUrl`. Both expire, so fetch them per session.

rxet never writes the token into an error message.

## Quick Start

Get three things from the Hub before you call rxet: the CAS endpoint, the file's Merkle hash, and its exact byte size. The endpoint and short-lived token come from the Hub's `xet-read-token` endpoint (`casUrl` and `accessToken` in the JSON reply); the hash and size come from the file metadata.

```r
library(rxet)

# From the Hub's xet-read-token response
endpoint <- "https://cas-server.xethub.hf.co"
cas_token <- "<accessToken>"

client <- xet_client_new(endpoint, cas_token)

hash <- "9f2c1d..." # Merkle hash from the Hub file metadata
size <- 1048576     # exact size in bytes

xet_download_file(client, hash = hash, file_size = size, dest_path = "model.parquet")
```

### Read into memory

```r
bytes <- xet_stream_raw(client, file_hash = hash, file_size = size)

# Or a byte range: [start_byte, end_byte), 0-indexed
footer <- xet_stream_range(
  client,
  file_hash = hash,
  file_size = size,
  start_byte = size - 65536,
  end_byte = size
)
```

There is no size cap. The `raw()` vector is allocated at full size before the download starts, so a file that does not fit fails immediately instead of part way through. rxet holds one copy of the bytes; a reader on top (Arrow, terra) adds its own.

### Parquet and geospatial files

```r
# Arrow; col_select drives selective range reads
df <- read_xet_parquet(client, file_hash = hash, file_size = size, col_select = c("id", "value"))

# terra; downloads to a file, so the bytes stay off the R heap
dem <- read_xet_raster(client, file_hash = hash, file_size = size)

# sf/GDAL; same, and single-file formats only, since the temp file has no extension
v <- read_xet_vector(client, file_hash = hash, file_size = size, ext = "gpkg")
```

`read_xet_parquet()` reads through `xet_open_stream_connection()`, a seekable connection that fetches Xet byte ranges on demand; unselected columns are not logically read, though aligned readahead may transfer some bytes. `read_xet_parquet()` streams; the raster and vector helpers download the whole file. `read_xet_raster()` also accepts a `dest_path = ` argument to save to a specific path instead of a session temporary file.

### Other streaming readers

```r
conn <- xet_open_stream_connection(client, file_hash = hash, file_size = size)
arrow::read_parquet(conn)   # or readBin(conn, "raw", 1024), seek(conn, ...)

xet_client_close(client)
```

Call `xet_client_close()` when you finish. In a function, register it with `on.exit()` so an error still releases the handle.

The connection is binary and seekable. Each miss fetches a window of at least 1 MiB (larger while reads move forward, up to 16 MiB), aligned to 64 KiB, and up to 64 MiB of windows are kept per connection. A file with 40 columns where you read 3 transfers roughly the footer plus the chunks for those 3 columns, plus readahead.

## Configuration

Set timeouts, cache size, and the performance preset when you create the client:

```r
client <- xet_client_new(
  endpoint, token,
  timeout_sec = 600, # network read timeout
  cache_bytes = 0,   # disable the chunk cache
  high_perf = TRUE   # hf-xet high-performance preset
)
```

- `NULL` (the default) for `timeout_sec` or `cache_bytes` leaves the hf-xet value alone, so the matching environment variable or the built-in default applies.
- An explicit argument overrides the environment variable for the field it sets.
- `high_perf = TRUE` raises concurrency and download buffer sizes. It does not touch the cache, and it overrides the environment because it is applied last.

Environment variables hf-xet reads when the argument is `NULL`:

- `HF_XET_CLIENT_READ_TIMEOUT`: network read timeout, default 300s
- `HF_XET_CHUNK_CACHE_SIZE_BYTES`: chunk cache size, default 10 GiB
- `HF_XET_HIGH_PERFORMANCE`: performance preset, default `false`

## API

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `xet_client_new(endpoint, token, timeout_sec, cache_bytes, high_perf)` | Create a handle |
| `xet_client_close(handle)` | Release a handle |
| `xet_download_file(handle, hash, file_size, dest_path)` | Download to disk |
| `xet_upload_file(handle, src_path)` | Upload a file, return hash and size |
| `xet_stream_raw(handle, file_hash, file_size)` | Whole file as `raw()` |
| `xet_stream_range(handle, file_hash, file_size, start_byte, end_byte)` | Byte range as `raw()` |
| `xet_open_connection(handle, file_hash, file_size)` | Whole file as an in-memory connection |
| `xet_open_stream_connection(handle, file_hash, file_size)` | Seekable connection over Xet ranges |
| `read_xet_parquet(handle, file_hash, file_size, ...)` | Read Parquet with arrow |
| `read_xet_raster(handle, file_hash, file_size, dest_path = NULL)` | Read a raster with terra |
| `read_xet_vector(handle, file_hash, file_size, ext = NULL, ...)` | Read a vector file with sf |

`xet_client_new()` and `xet_client_close()` are Supported. The other nine are Experimental; see the support status section.

## Architecture

Three layers:

1. Rust (`src/rust/src/lib.rs`): the Xet client and download pipeline.
2. extendr bindings (`src/rust/src/lib.rs`): FFI to R.
3. R wrappers (`R/*.R`): argument checks and optional-package helpers.

Handles are UUID strings. A `Registry<T>` (`src/rust/src/registry.rs`) maps each handle to its client behind a mutex, and reports a poisoned lock as an error rather than as an unknown handle. Panics are caught with `std::panic::catch_unwind()`.

Memory: `xet_stream_raw()`, `xet_stream_range()`, and `xet_open_connection()` hold the bytes in one R vector. `xet_download_file()` writes straight to disk, and `read_xet_raster()` and `read_xet_vector()` use it, so their bytes never enter R memory. `xet_open_stream_connection()` holds only its readahead windows.

The lazy connection needs a custom R connection type, because R has no way to define one from R code. That class lives in `src/connection.c`; its read callback calls back into Rust through `xet_reader_read()`.

## Benchmarking

rxet makes no throughput claims. Measure your own workload:

```sh
Rscript tools/benchmark.R models.json
Rscript tools/benchmark-extended.R models.json --memory --workers
```

See `tools/README.md`.

## Testing

```r
devtools::test()
```

The routine suite runs offline. Fault tests (`test-fault-midstream.R`, `test-fault-token.R`) start a loopback fault server in a `processx` child process and need no token or network. Upload and round-trip tests need the upstream `local_cas_server`:

```sh
cargo install xet-client --version 1.7.0 --features simulation --bin local_cas_server --locked
export RXET_LOCAL_CAS_SERVER="$(command -v local_cas_server)"
```

Without it, those tests skip. Live tests are off by default; they need `RXET_LIVE_TESTS=1` and `HF_TOKEN` with read access to `brownag/rxet-test-data`, and they run only on demand, never in public CI. Public CI runs the local-server suite.

## Support status

| Function | Tier |
|---|---|
| `xet_client_new`, `xet_client_close` | Supported |
| `xet_download_file`, `xet_upload_file` | Experimental |
| `xet_stream_raw`, `xet_stream_range`, `xet_open_connection` | Experimental |
| `xet_open_stream_connection` | Experimental (needs R >= 4.3) |
| `read_xet_parquet`, `read_xet_raster`, `read_xet_vector` | Experimental |

Experimental functions are exported and usable. They are covered by the offline and local-server suites; the transfer functions also by the on-demand live suite. The tier reflects the evidence available, not an intent to change the API.

See [NEWS.md](NEWS.md) for release notes.
